chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Fudayl's brother, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Among the sins that are not forgiven is a person's saying: 'I wish I was not held accountable for any deeds other than this one.'
ai.seo_question: What is a sin that is not forgiven according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this specific sin as a subtle form of spiritual arrogance where one minimizes the weight of their transgressions by fixating on a single virtue, thereby rejecting the holistic nature of divine justice. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accounting), warning that such selective pride obstructs the comprehensive mercy of Allah. The narration serves as a practical reminder to maintain humility in both good deeds and sins, acknowledging that all actions are subject to God's complete judgment.
